Welcome
Welcome to Tolworth School. Thank you for taking the time to get to know us a little better. Tolworth School is a federation that formally links Tolworth Infant and Nursery School with Tolworth Junior School. The schools are attached in one building and work as one school, with one Headteacher and one Governing Body. Our Nursery provides the equivalent of 52 part-time places for 3-4 year olds with some of these places allocated as full 30 hour places. We also have a small number of 2 year old places. Reception and Years One to Six each have three classes of up to 30 children.
The school is tucked safely behind Tolworth Broadway, away from the noise and traffic of the main road, with plenty of green space available to us for play and learning. We have a close relationship with Tolworth Children’s Centre, which shares our site. We are a positive and vibrant community school where ‘happy children, successful learners’ is our motto. We work hard to nurture and support every child so that they can reach their full potential, while enjoying their learning journey.
This website has been designed to answer as many of your questions as possible however, we are always happy to show you round. If you require paper copies of any information on our website please contact the school office.
Mrs Rachel Seivright Nye, Headteacher

Reception Parents - Intake September 2026
Reception Parents - Intake September 2026
We look forward to welcoming you and your child to Tolworth School in September and are delighted that you have chosen us. Your child has been allocated a full time place in one of our Reception classes by the Local Authority and we hope your family will enjoy being part of our school community.
Early in May you will be emailed a Tolworth School Pupil Admission Form. Please return it to the School Office or email it back to us at admin@tins.rbksch.org A paper copy of the Tolworth Pupil Admission Form can also be collected from the school office.
If your child has a food allergy or intolerance it is important that you clearly highlight this on the Pupil Admission Form as our caterers, will need you to complete an additional form, in order that your child is served food that is safe for them to eat.
We will also need to see your child's Birth Certificate or Passport for verification, before your child starts with us. Please bring this with the Admissions Form. We will be holding a New to Reception Parents Evening (adults only please) on Wednesday 17th June starting at 6.45pm. You can bring your child’s Birth Certificate or Passport to this meeting too or to one of the Transition Days, we can take a photocopy for our records and give it back to you.
The New Reception Parents Evening is an opportunity for you to learn more about our school, including how we will help your child to settle in and some of the ways in which we teach. You may start the evening by meeting your child’s teacher and viewing the classroom. At 7pm there will be a short talk by Rachel Nye, Headteacher, followed by a further opportunity to ask about uniform, school meals and other aspects of school life which you may wish to find out about. You may visit your child’s classroom before or after the talk. The evening should close by 8.15pm.
We would appreciate it if children are not brought to this meeting as your child will have a chance to spend time in school on our Transition Days. We are holding TWO transition taster sessions this year, which will give your child time in school to meet their teacher, other staff in the Reception and some classmates.
The dates and times are below:
Wednesday 1st July 2026
9.15 am – 10.15 am (for children currently attending Tolworth School Nursery)
10.30 am – 11.30 am (for all other children joining Reception)
Friday 4th September 2026
9.30 am – 10.30 am (for all children joining Reception)
1.30 pm – 2.30 pm (for all children joining Reception)
Your child can attend on both the dates above. You do not need to book but please attend the correct session.

SEND (Special Educational Needs and/or Disabilities) Information
Our school is proud of our strong inclusive values and ethos, where happy children can be successful learners. We strive to enable our pupils to reach their full potential through creating a rich and diverse learning environment and an atmosphere of encouragement, acceptance and respect that is sensitive to individual needs.
When a child is identified as having a learning, physical, behavioural or emotional difficulty that requires special educational provision to be made then this is described as Special Educational Needs and/or Disability (“SEND”). The school has a Specialist Resourced Provision (SRP) for children who have identified moderate to severe learning needs, including global developmental delay, Down’s Syndrome and other genetic conditions that affect their learning.
Some children at our school may be identified as requiring additional support in at least one of the following four areas:
The principle of early identification and intervention underpins our approach to identifying those pupils who need extra help. Sometimes, despite high quality first teaching and additional support, some pupils may continue to make insufficient progress; in these instances we may need to consult with outside agencies to receive more specialised expertise, such as that available through Educational Psychology Service, Speech and Language Therapy, Occupational Therapy, Physiotherapy and the School Health Team.
For more information on all that we offer children with a Special Educational Need and/or Disability, please download our full SEND Information Report below. Should you require paper copies of any of our policies or documents please do not hesitate to contact us and we will be happy to post them to you.
Alternatively please contact Mrs Baker our Junior SENCo (Juniors: Year 3 - Year 6) at: Junior SENCo or Mrs Dodson our Infant SENCo (Infants: Nursery Year 2) at: Infant SENCo
Send Local Officer for Kingston and Richmond - a website containing information about services and support for children and young people with special educational needs or disabilities, and their families, in Kingston and Richmond. www.kr.afcinfo.org.uk/local_offer
Kingston Parent Carer Forum Website: https://kingstonpcf.co.uk
SEND Information, Advice and Support (SENDIASS) Phone: 0808 164 5527 Email: info@rksendiass.co.uk

Special Educational Needs and Disability Register
All local authorities must have a record or register of children with Special Educational Needs and/or Disabilities (SEND) in their area. If you live in either Kingston or Richmond, we encourage anyone whose family includes a child or young person who has a special educational need or disability to register.
Everyone on the register will benefit from:
• Information about support, services, activities and events
• Information aimed at young people with disabilities
• Opportunities to have your say about the services that are important to you
• The knowledge that your anonymous statistical data is helping to plan and improve services
Find out more and register on the SEND Local Offer website

All children are eligible for 15 hours a week of free nursery education starting from the term after their third birthday. This is part of the Government’s ‘Universal entitlement’ through the early education funding scheme.
At Tolworth School, we offer places for three year olds from the September after they turn three. For full admission information on when and how to apply please click here
We offer places to families eligible for the extended entitlement which totals 30 hours per week (term time only) This extended entitlement is for working families in which neither parent earns more than £100,000 a year. For more information and to check your eligibility please visit www.childcarechoices.gov.uk
For an additional cost we also over wrap around care, which is subject to availability.

Pupil Premium at Tolworth
The Department for Education allocates the Pupil Premium Grant to schools. Pupils eligible for this grant are those who, currently or have claimed Free School Meals in the last six years, or who are looked after children.
The aim of the funding is to remove barriers to learning which may hinder children who fall under the pupil premium category. With these barriers removed, the gap in attainment between pupil premium children and their non-FSM peers should close. The reasons for under achievement can be many and varied. Reasons could include; less support at home, social and emotional difficulties due to complex family situations or attendance and punctuality difficulties. Each child entitled to the pupil premium grant is unique in their situation. Our responses to their need must reflect this and support will be personalised to ensure each child reaches their full potential.
Key initiatives put in place to remove barriers to learning
The progress and attainment of all pupils is carefully tracked and analysed in order to draw conclusions and develop action plans. We also make use of a wide range of educational research in order to decide how best to spend our funding and maximise the opportunities for our pupils.
The pupil premium strategy is a key focus of our school development plan and so has a consistently high profile within the school. At the core of our strategy are ‘quality first teaching practises’ which ensure that lessons meet the needs of each individual learner and the embedding of ‘meta-cognitive’ practises. These two initiatives in particular have led to a more aspirational culture of pupils, who have/or are developing, a growth mind-set toward their learning.
Each year, strategies are reviewed and successful strategies are embedded in the schools practice. Therefore only annual focus strategies appear in any particular pupil premium strategy statement (it is not an exhaustive list of all that we do).

Safeguarding is everybody’s responsibility
The Federation of Tolworth Schools is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of all children and adults at our school.
We expect all staff and volunteers to share in our commitment to keeping children safe and observe the wide range of safeguarding measures we have in place. All staff and regular volunteers have DBS checks and visitors are signposted to the designated safeguard leads, Rachel Seivright-Nye (Headteacher) and Linda Jackson (Children & Families Co-ordinator) through our safeguarding information and notices displayed around our school.

Keeping children safe during community activities, after-school clubs and tuition
At Tolworth School we are aware that some of our pupils are young carers. A young carer is someone aged 5-18 who is caring unpaid for a family member or friend who is ill, frail, disabled or has mental health or addiction problems. Tolworth School has successfully gained the Gold Young Carers in School Award which helps us to ensure we are identifying and offering the support that our young carers need.
If you think your child is a young carer and would like any other information or support please contact Linda Jackson, Children and Families Coordinator.
We respect the privacy of our young carers so will only share information about them with the people who need to know, so that they can offer help.
Linda Jackson (Children & Families Coordinator) can offer on-going support to families including parenting, providing advice, emotional support; help with attending meetings and signposting to other services.
Caring for children and young people can be challenging. It is important to seek support if needed in providing children with the necessary care and stimulation they need to help them thrive. If we identify that a child or family need any additional support we will assess and signpost to local support agencies, including making referrals to the Early Help Team in Kingston if needed.
If you need any help or support, just ask to speak to Linda Jackson at the school office or email ljacks8@tjs.rbksch.org
